dataNote: Coordinates are approximate town and landmark centroids. Fees and fares are editable estimates, not live prices. Alternate spellings are listed per place so search finds them.

destinations.name: Naran
destinations.tagline: Alpine lakes, glaciers and the road to Babusar
destinations.description: Naran sits at the head of the Kaghan Valley on the Kunhar River, and is the launch point for Saif-ul-Malook, Lulusar and the Babusar Top crossing into Gilgit-Baltistan. The road is snow-closed from roughly November to April.

attractions.name: Lake Saif-ul-Malook
attractions.description: Glacial lake at 3,224 m below Malika Parbat. The last 9 km is a rough jeep track.

attractions.name: Lulusar Lake
attractions.description: Source of the Kunhar River, sitting right beside the Babusar road at 3,410 m.

attractions.name: Babusar Top
attractions.description: A 4,173 m pass linking Kaghan to the Karakoram Highway. Open July to September in most years.

attractions.name: Ansoo Lake
attractions.description: Tear-shaped lake reached by a demanding full-day trek from Saif-ul-Malook. A guide is strongly advised.

attractions.name: Shogran
attractions.description: Forested plateau at 2,362 m, the staging point for the Siri Paye jeep track.

attractions.name: Siri Paye Meadows
attractions.description: High meadow above Shogran with Makra Peak views. Jeep only, roughly 8 km of track.

destinations.name: Hunza (Karimabad)
destinations.tagline: Forts, cherry blossom and the Karakoram skyline
destinations.description: Karimabad looks straight onto Rakaposhi and Ultar Sar, with two restored forts above the bazaar. It is reached on the Karakoram Highway, which is paved the whole way from Islamabad.

attractions.name: Baltit Fort
attractions.description: A 700-year-old fort above Karimabad, restored by the Aga Khan Trust. Guided entry only.

attractions.name: Altit Fort
attractions.description: The older of the two Hunza forts, with a restored royal garden beside it.

attractions.name: Attabad Lake
attractions.description: Turquoise lake formed by the 2010 landslide. Boat and jet-ski rentals sit on the KKH shore.

attractions.name: Passu Cones
attractions.description: Serrated peaks beside the KKH, with the Hussaini suspension bridge a short walk away.

attractions.name: Khunjerab Pass
attractions.description: A 4,693 m China border crossing inside Khunjerab National Park. A park fee applies per person.

attractions.name: Eagle Nest, Duikar
attractions.description: Sunrise and sunset viewpoint above Karimabad taking in Rakaposhi, Diran and Golden Peak.

destinations.name: Skardu
destinations.tagline: Cold desert, Deosai and the gateway to K2
destinations.description: Skardu sits in a broad Indus valley ringed by the Karakoram, and is the road head for Deosai, Shigar and the Baltoro treks. Flights from Islamabad exist but are weather-dependent.

attractions.name: Lower Kachura (Shangrila) Lake
attractions.description: Heart-shaped lake inside the Shangrila resort grounds, 20 km from Skardu.

attractions.name: Upper Kachura Lake
attractions.description: A deeper, quieter lake a short walk beyond Shangrila.

attractions.name: Deosai National Park
attractions.description: A 4,114 m plateau with Sheosar Lake and brown bear habitat. Full-day 4x4 trip, snow-free July to September.

attractions.name: Katpana Cold Desert
attractions.description: High-altitude sand dunes beside the Indus, minutes from Skardu airport.

attractions.name: Shigar Fort
attractions.description: A 17th-century Raja fort restored as a heritage hotel, 32 km from Skardu.

attractions.name: Manthokha Waterfall
attractions.description: A 55 m waterfall in Kharmang, about 80 km from Skardu.

destinations.name: Fairy Meadows
destinations.tagline: Nanga Parbat from a meadow you can only walk to
destinations.description: A grass shelf facing the Nanga Parbat north face. Access is a jeep ride from Raikot Bridge to Tato, then a 3 to 4 hour walk or pony ride. No road reaches the meadow itself.

attractions.name: Raikot Bridge Jeep Stand
attractions.description: KKH jeep stand. Shared or reserved jeep up the Raikot track to Tato village.

attractions.name: Beyal Camp
attractions.description: A two-hour walk beyond Fairy Meadows toward the glacier, with closer Nanga Parbat views.

attractions.name: Nanga Parbat Base Camp
attractions.description: Full-day return trek from Fairy Meadows to the Rakhiot face base camp at about 3,967 m.

destinations.name: Swat (Mingora)
destinations.tagline: Buddhist ruins, ski slopes and the Upper Swat road
destinations.description: Mingora is the valley base, reached by the Swat Expressway from Islamabad in roughly four hours. Malam Jabba and the Kalam road branch north from here.

attractions.name: Malam Jabba Ski Resort
attractions.description: Pakistan's main ski resort at 2,804 m, with a chairlift and zipline running year round.

attractions.name: Kalam
attractions.description: Upper Swat town at 2,000 m where the Ushu and Utror rivers meet. Roughly 3 hours from Mingora.

attractions.name: Mahodand Lake
attractions.description: Lake of fishes, 35 km beyond Kalam on a rough track through Ushu Forest. Jeep required.

attractions.name: Butkara Stupa
attractions.description: A 2nd-century BCE Buddhist stupa complex on the edge of Mingora.

attractions.name: White Palace, Marghazar
attractions.description: Marble summer palace of the Wali of Swat, built in 1940 about 13 km from Saidu Sharif.

destinations.name: Kumrat Valley
destinations.tagline: Deodar forest and river camping in Upper Dir
destinations.description: Kumrat is a forested valley on the Panjkora River above Thal, with camping rather than hotels as the norm. The last stretch from Thal is an unpaved jeep track.

attractions.name: Kala Chashma
attractions.description: Cold spring and picnic spot in deodar forest inside the main Kumrat valley.

attractions.name: Jahaz Banda Meadows
attractions.description: High meadow reached by jeep to Badgoi then a 2 hour walk. Common overnight camp.

attractions.name: Katora Lake
attractions.description: Bowl-shaped alpine lake, a hard 3 hour climb above Jahaz Banda.

attractions.name: Kumrat Waterfall
attractions.description: Roadside waterfall near the upper camping grounds of the valley.

destinations.name: Neelum Valley (Keran)
destinations.tagline: A river valley pressed against the Line of Control
destinations.description: The Neelum river road runs 200 km from Muzaffarabad past Keran and Sharda to Kel. Several stretches are single-lane and landsliding is common after rain.

attractions.name: Ratti Gali Lake
attractions.description: Alpine lake at 3,700 m above Dowarian. Jeep to base camp then a 2 hour climb.

attractions.name: Arang Kel
attractions.description: Hilltop village above Kel, reached by chairlift and then a steep 40 minute walk.

attractions.name: Sharda
attractions.description: Riverside town holding the ruins of the Sharda Peeth temple and university.

attractions.name: Kutton (Jagran) Waterfall
attractions.description: Waterfall and trout stream in a side valley about 25 km before Keran.

destinations.name: Murree
destinations.tagline: The closest hill station to the capital
destinations.description: Murree is about 60 km from Islamabad on the expressway and fills up fast on weekends and during snowfall. Best treated as a one or two night stop rather than a base.

attractions.name: Mall Road
attractions.description: Pedestrian bazaar with colonial-era buildings, cafes and viewpoints at both ends.

attractions.name: Patriata (New Murree)
attractions.description: Chairlift and cable car to a 2,274 m ridge, 15 km south of Murree.

attractions.name: Kashmir Point
attractions.description: North-facing viewpoint looking toward the Pir Panjal range on clear days.

attractions.name: Ayubia National Park
attractions.description: Pine reserve with a chairlift and the Pipeline Track walk to Dunga Gali.

attractions.name: Panj Peer Rocks
attractions.description: A pair of rock outcrops above Kotli Sattian with a long view over the Margalla and Murree ridges. About 25 km from Murree, then a 30 minute walk up from the road.

destinations.name: Nathia Gali
destinations.tagline: Pine ridges and short summit walks
destinations.description: A quieter alternative to Murree on the Abbottabad side of the Galiyat, with well-marked walking tracks to Mushkpuri and Miranjani.

attractions.name: Mushkpuri Top
attractions.description: A 2,800 m summit, a 4 km walk up from Dunga Gali through pine and oak forest.

attractions.name: Miranjani Top
attractions.description: The highest point in the Galiyat at 2,992 m, reached from behind Nathia Gali bazaar.

attractions.name: Pipeline Track
attractions.description: Level 4 km forest walk between Nathia Gali and Dunga Gali along an old water pipeline.

attractions.name: St Matthew's Church
attractions.description: Wooden church built in 1914 in the middle of the Nathia Gali bazaar.

destinations.name: Gilgit
destinations.tagline: The junction town of three mountain ranges
destinations.description: Gilgit is where the Karakoram, Hindu Kush and Himalaya meet, and the main resupply stop between Hunza, Skardu and Chitral.

attractions.name: Naltar Valley
attractions.description: Coloured lakes and a ski slope, 40 km up a rough jeep track from Gilgit.

attractions.name: Rakaposhi View Point
attractions.description: KKH cafe stop at Ghulmet looking directly at the 7,788 m Rakaposhi face.

attractions.name: Kargah Buddha
attractions.description: A 7th-century Buddha carved into a cliff 10 km west of Gilgit.

destinations.name: Chitral
destinations.tagline: Hindu Kush valleys and the Kalash calendar
destinations.description: Chitral town sits under Tirich Mir on the Chitral River. Access from the south is through the Lowari Tunnel, which keeps the route open in winter.

attractions.name: Bumburet, Kalash Valley
attractions.description: Largest of the three Kalash valleys, 36 km from Chitral. A tourist permit fee applies.

attractions.name: Rumbur Valley
attractions.description: Quieter Kalash valley north of Bumburet, reached on a narrow jeep road.

attractions.name: Shandur Pass
attractions.description: A 3,700 m pass with the world's highest polo ground, 160 km east of Chitral on a rough road.

attractions.name: Chitral Fort and Shahi Masjid
attractions.description: Riverside fort of the Mehtars of Chitral, beside the 1924 Shahi Mosque.

destinations.name: Muzaffarabad
destinations.tagline: Where the Neelum meets the Jhelum
destinations.description: The AJK capital, sitting at the confluence of two rivers and the entry point for both the Neelum and Jhelum valley roads.

attractions.name: Pir Chinasi
attractions.description: A 2,900 m ridge shrine 30 km east of the city, with views over the whole Jhelum valley.

attractions.name: Red Fort (Muzaffarabad Fort)
attractions.description: A 16th-century Chak dynasty fort on the bank of the Neelum River.

attractions.name: Subri Lake
attractions.description: Reservoir lake south of the city with boating and lakeside restaurants.

destinations.name: Islamabad
destinations.tagline: Margalla foothills and the country's cleanest streets
destinations.description: A planned city below the Margalla Hills, and the practical staging point for every northern route. Most sights sit inside a 30 km radius.

attractions.name: Faisal Mosque
attractions.description: Tent-shaped mosque at the foot of the Margallas, completed in 1986.

attractions.name: Daman-e-Koh
attractions.description: Margalla terrace viewpoint looking down the length of the city grid.

attractions.name: Taxila Museum and Ruins
attractions.description: Gandharan archaeological sites and museum, 35 km west on the GT Road.

attractions.name: Rawal Lake
attractions.description: Reservoir with a lakeside park and boating, between Islamabad and Rawalpindi.

attractions.name: Khewra Salt Mine
attractions.description: The world's second-largest salt mine, 160 km south on the M2. Train ride into the tunnels.

destinations.name: Lahore
destinations.tagline: Mughal monuments and the country's loudest food street
destinations.description: The Walled City holds the densest cluster of Mughal-era buildings in Pakistan. Everything below sits within a 25 km radius of the centre.

attractions.name: Badshahi Mosque
attractions.description: Aurangzeb's 1673 mosque facing the fort across Hazuri Bagh.

attractions.name: Lahore Fort
attractions.description: UNESCO-listed citadel holding the Sheesh Mahal and Naulakha Pavilion.

attractions.name: Shalimar Gardens
attractions.description: Terraced Mughal garden built in 1642 on the Grand Trunk Road.

attractions.name: Wagah Border Ceremony
attractions.description: Evening flag-lowering parade at the India border, 25 km east of the city.

attractions.name: Fort Road Food Street
attractions.description: Rooftop restaurants inside the Walled City facing Badshahi Mosque.

destinations.name: Multan
destinations.tagline: City of saints and blue tilework
destinations.description: Multan's old city is built around a mound of Sufi shrines, most of them faced in the blue and turquoise tile the region is known for.

attractions.name: Tomb of Shah Rukn-e-Alam
attractions.description: A 14th-century octagonal brick tomb on the Multan Fort mound.

attractions.name: Shrine of Bahauddin Zakariya
attractions.description: A 13th-century Suhrawardi shrine, the oldest on the fort mound.

attractions.name: Multan Fort (Qasim Bagh)
attractions.description: Remains of the old citadel, now a public park above the bazaars.

attractions.name: Hussain Agahi Bazaar
attractions.description: Old-city market for blue pottery, khussa shoes and camel-skin lamps.

destinations.name: Karachi
destinations.tagline: The port city, its beaches and its food
destinations.description: Pakistan's largest city and the main Arabian Sea port. Sights are spread out, so budget for local transport between them.

attractions.name: Clifton Beach
attractions.description: The city's main urban beach, busiest at sunset and on weekends.

attractions.name: Mohatta Palace Museum
attractions.description: A 1927 Rajasthani-stone palace in Clifton, now an exhibition museum.

attractions.name: Mazar-e-Quaid
attractions.description: The white marble mausoleum of Muhammad Ali Jinnah, set in a large park.

attractions.name: Manora Island
attractions.description: Peninsula reached by ferry from Keamari, with a lighthouse and quiet beaches.

attractions.name: Empress Market
attractions.description: An 1889 colonial market hall in Saddar, still the city's main produce bazaar.

destinations.name: Kund Malir & Hingol
destinations.tagline: Desert cliffs meeting the Arabian Sea
destinations.description: A beach on the Makran Coastal Highway inside Hingol National Park, about 240 km west of Karachi. There are no hotels, so most visitors day-trip or camp.

attractions.name: Kund Malir Beach
attractions.description: Wide sand beach below desert hills, directly on the coastal highway.

attractions.name: Princess of Hope
attractions.description: Wind-carved rock formation beside the highway inside Hingol National Park.

attractions.name: Chandragup Mud Volcano
attractions.description: Active mud volcano and Hindu pilgrimage site, reached on a short desert track.

attractions.name: Buzi Pass
attractions.description: Highway pass through eroded badlands, the most photographed stretch of the route.

destinations.name: Gwadar
destinations.tagline: A hammerhead peninsula on the Arabian Sea
destinations.description: Gwadar sits on a tombolo between two bays, backed by the Koh-e-Batil ridge. It is a long drive from Karachi, so most visitors fly or break the journey at Kund Malir.

attractions.name: Koh-e-Batil Viewpoint
attractions.description: Flat-topped ridge above the port with views over both bays.

attractions.name: Astola Island
attractions.description: Pakistan's largest offshore island, a 5 hour boat trip from Pasni. Camping only.

attractions.name: Gwadar West Bay
attractions.description: Long crescent beach on the western side of the peninsula.

destinations.name: Ziarat & Quetta
destinations.tagline: The world's second-largest juniper forest
destinations.description: Ziarat is a 2,450 m hill town 120 km east of Quetta, surrounded by juniper stands that are several thousand years old.

attractions.name: Quaid-e-Azam Residency
attractions.description: Wooden colonial residency where Jinnah spent his final months, rebuilt after 2013.

attractions.name: Ziarat Juniper Forest
attractions.description: Protected juniper stand, with individual trees estimated at over 4,000 years old.

attractions.name: Hanna Lake
attractions.description: Reservoir in the Urak valley 10 km from Quetta, with boating and a lakeside island.

attractions.name: Hazarganji-Chiltan National Park
attractions.description: Mountain park south-west of Quetta protecting the Chiltan wild goat.

destinations.name: Thandiani
destinations.tagline: A cold pine ridge above Abbottabad
destinations.description: Thandiani sits at 2,750 m on a forested ridge 31 km east of Abbottabad, and is the quietest of the Galiyat hill stations. The name means "very cold". The approach road is narrow and unlit, so it is normally done as a daylight run.

attractions.name: Thandiani Top
attractions.description: The ridge itself, looking east to the Kashmir mountains and north to Nanga Parbat on a clear morning.

attractions.name: Thandiani Forest Trail
attractions.description: An easy walk through pine and fir along the ridge, with no facilities beyond the parking area.

attractions.name: Ilyasi Mosque
attractions.description: A spring-fed mosque at Nawanshehr on the Abbottabad side, known for the food stalls around it.

attractions.name: Harnoi
attractions.description: A stream and picnic spot on the road up from Abbottabad, busy on weekends.

attractions.name: Shimla Peak
attractions.description: A short climb above Abbottabad city with a view over the whole valley.

destinations.name: Rawalakot
destinations.tagline: Pine bowls and lake picnics in Poonch
destinations.description: Rawalakot lies in a wide bowl of terraced fields and pine at 1,638 m, and is the base for Banjosa and the Toli Peer ridge. Roughly a four hour drive from Islamabad.

attractions.name: Banjosa Lake
attractions.description: An artificial lake ringed by pine at 1,981 m, 18 km from Rawalakot, with boating and a rest house.

attractions.name: Toli Peer
attractions.description: A 2,743 m grass ridge 30 km from Rawalakot, the last stretch on a rough jeep track.

attractions.name: Devi Gali
attractions.description: A roadside pass on the Banjosa road with views back over the Rawalakot bowl.

destinations.name: Astore & Rama
destinations.tagline: The quiet side of Nanga Parbat
destinations.description: Astore town sits on the road between the Karakoram Highway and Deosai. Rama, 11 km above it, is a pine meadow and lake facing the Nanga Parbat ice.

attractions.name: Rama Lake
attractions.description: A glacial lake above Rama meadow at about 3,300 m, reached by jeep then a short walk.

attractions.name: Rama Meadow
attractions.description: Pine-ringed grass at 3,000 m with the standard camping ground and a PTDC rest house.

attractions.name: Rupal Face
attractions.description: The 4,600 m south wall of Nanga Parbat, the highest mountain face on earth, reached via Tarashing.

attractions.name: Minimarg
attractions.description: A meadow valley beyond Domail on the Burzil road, close to the Line of Control. Permit territory.

destinations.name: Phander Valley
destinations.tagline: Blue water and poplars on the Gilgit river
destinations.description: Phander sits at 2,900 m on the Gilgit to Chitral road, a string of blue lake pools between poplar stands. The road onward over Shandur is seasonal.

attractions.name: Phander Lake
attractions.description: The main lake beside the road, known for trout and for the viewpoint above the bend.

attractions.name: Khalti Lake
attractions.description: A wide lake at Gupis, 60 km before Phander, which freezes hard enough to walk on in winter.

attractions.name: Handrap Lake
attractions.description: A side-valley lake above Phander, reached on a rough track then a walk.

attractions.name: Shandur Pass from Phander
attractions.description: The 3,700 m polo ground pass, about 75 km west of Phander on an unpaved road.

destinations.name: Khanpur Lake
destinations.tagline: Islamabad’s nearest water day trip
destinations.description: A reservoir on the Haro River about 40 km from Islamabad, and the closest place to the capital for boating, cliff jumping and kayaking. Comfortably a day trip.

attractions.name: Khanpur Lake Shore
attractions.description: The main jetty area, where boats, jet skis and kayaks are hired by the hour.

attractions.name: Cliff Diving Point
attractions.description: A run of managed jumping platforms with kayaks and zip lines, charged as a day pass.

attractions.name: Shah Allah Ditta Caves
attractions.description: Buddhist-era caves and a banyan grove on the far side of the Margallas, on the way back.

destinations.name: Soon Valley
destinations.tagline: Salt Range lakes and orchards
destinations.description: A green valley in the Salt Range about 220 km from Islamabad, with three brackish lakes that pull flamingos in winter. Reachable in an ordinary car.

attractions.name: Khabeki Lake
attractions.description: A shallow salt lake below Sakesar, the easiest of the three to reach.

attractions.name: Uchhali Lake
attractions.description: The largest of the Salt Range lakes, a wintering site for flamingos and cranes.

attractions.name: Sakesar
attractions.description: At 1,522 m the highest point of the Salt Range, with a view over all three lakes.

attractions.name: Kanhatti Garden
attractions.description: A spring-fed orchard garden with a small waterfall, popular for picnics.

destinations.name: Thatta & Keenjhar
destinations.tagline: A necropolis, a tiled mosque and a lake
destinations.description: Thatta lies about 100 km east of Karachi and holds the Makli necropolis, one of the largest burial grounds anywhere, alongside Shah Jahan’s tiled mosque.

attractions.name: Makli Necropolis
attractions.description: A UNESCO site of half a million tombs spread over 10 km² of ridge, built between the 14th and 18th centuries.

attractions.name: Shah Jahan Mosque
attractions.description: A 1647 mosque faced in blue Sindhi tile, with 93 domes and no minarets.

attractions.name: Keenjhar Lake
attractions.description: Pakistan’s largest freshwater lake and Karachi’s water supply, with boating along the near shore.

attractions.name: Ranikot Fort
attractions.description: The Great Wall of Sindh: a 30 km circuit of rampart in the Kirthar hills, about 180 km north of Thatta.

destinations.name: Peshawar
destinations.tagline: Storytellers’ bazaar and the Khyber road
destinations.description: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in South Asia, at the eastern end of the Khyber Pass. The walled city, the museum and the food are the draw.

attractions.name: Qissa Khwani Bazaar
attractions.description: The storytellers’ bazaar in the old city, the traditional caravan stop and still the best street food.

attractions.name: Peshawar Museum
attractions.description: Holds one of the world’s largest collections of Gandharan Buddhist sculpture.

attractions.name: Bala Hisar Fort
attractions.description: The fort on the mound above the city, occupied in some form since the Durrani period.

attractions.name: Sethi House
attractions.description: A 19th-century merchant house in Mohalla Sethian, built with Bukhara-style woodwork and a basement for the heat.

attractions.name: Khyber Pass
attractions.description: The historic pass toward Torkham. Entry beyond Jamrud needs a permit and normally an escort — arrange it before you go.

destinations.name: Bahawalpur & Cholistan
destinations.tagline: Nawabi palaces and a fort in the sand
destinations.description: Bahawalpur was a princely state, and its palaces still stand at the edge of the Cholistan desert. Derawar Fort, 100 km out in the sand, is the reason most people come.

attractions.name: Noor Mahal
attractions.description: An 1872 Italianate palace built for the Nawab of Bahawalpur, now army-managed and open to visitors.

attractions.name: Derawar Fort
attractions.description: Forty square bastions rising out of the Cholistan sand, about 100 km south of Bahawalpur. 4x4 and a local driver strongly advised.

attractions.name: Lal Suhanra National Park
attractions.description: A biosphere reserve of desert, wetland and forest, with a blackbuck and blue bull breeding programme.

attractions.name: Darbar Mahal
attractions.description: The 1905 court palace of the state, a short drive from Noor Mahal.

destinations.name: Khaplu
destinations.tagline: Little Tibet on the upper Shyok
destinations.description: Khaplu is the old capital of the Yabgo rajas, 103 km east of Skardu on the Shyok River, and the road head for the Hushe valley and the Masherbrum approaches.

attractions.name: Khaplu Palace
attractions.description: An 1840 raja’s palace restored by the Aga Khan Trust, now a museum and hotel.

attractions.name: Chaqchan Mosque
attractions.description: Built in 1370 when the valley converted to Islam, in a Tibetan-Kashmiri timber style.

attractions.name: Hushe Valley
attractions.description: The trekking corridor toward Masherbrum and K6, about 80 km north of Khaplu on a rough road.

attractions.name: Saling Nallah
attractions.description: A side valley of apricot orchards and terraces, an easy half day from town.

destinations.name: Nagar & Hopar
destinations.tagline: Glacier country across the river from Hunza
destinations.description: Nagar faces Hunza across the river and holds the Hopar glacier bowl and the walk up to Rush Lake, one of the highest alpine lakes anywhere.

attractions.name: Hopar Glacier
attractions.description: A bowl of grey ice below Golden Peak, about 10 km up from Nagar Khas.

attractions.name: Rush Lake
attractions.description: At 4,694 m one of the highest alpine lakes on earth, a two to three day trek from Hopar. Not a day trip.

attractions.name: Rakaposhi Base Camp
attractions.description: A long day’s walk up from Minapin to the glacier viewpoint under the 7,788 m north face.

destinations.name: Katas Raj & Kallar Kahar
destinations.tagline: Salt Range temples on the motorway
destinations.description: A cluster of Hindu temples around a sacred pool in the Salt Range, right off the M2 between Islamabad and Lahore. Easily combined with Khewra as one long day.

attractions.name: Katas Raj Temples
attractions.description: Temples of the Shri Katas Raj complex around a spring-fed pool, parts dating to the 6th century.

attractions.name: Kallar Kahar
attractions.description: A salt lake and peacock-populated garden beside the motorway interchange.

attractions.name: Khewra Salt Mine
attractions.description: The world’s second-largest salt mine, with a narrow-gauge train into the tunnels. 35 km from Katas Raj.

destinations.name: Ormara
destinations.tagline: An empty hammerhead beach halfway to Gwadar
destinations.description: Ormara sits on a tombolo on the Makran Coastal Highway, roughly halfway between Karachi and Gwadar. Long empty beaches, very little infrastructure, so most people camp.

attractions.name: Ormara East Beach
attractions.description: A wide sand crescent on the eastern side of the peninsula, usually empty on weekdays.

attractions.name: Ras Ormara Head
attractions.description: The rocky headland at the tip of the tombolo, with a view along both bays.

attractions.name: Turtle Nesting Beach
attractions.description: Green turtles nest along this stretch between September and January. Do not use lights near the sand at night.
